history.period: 1851 CE (Ratan Bihari); reign of Sardar Singh, 1851-1872 (Rasik Shiromani)
history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2134 ('Ratan Bihari Temple', Bikaner) is a confirmed duplicate of seq 2068 ('Ratan Bihari & Rasik Shiromani Temples', id 'ratan-bihari-rasik-shiromani-temples-bikaner') - the same temple complex: travel sources (rajasthandhara.com) describe Ratan Bihari Ji and Rasik Shiromani Ji as one combined temple. Deduplicate downstream. Ratan Bihari Temple was built by Maharaja Ratan Singh (1828-1851): the foundation was laid on the 3rd day of the bright half of Falgun, Samvat 1907 (1851 AD), and completed by his successor son Maharaja Surat Singh. Krishna/Vishnu temples were rare in Bikaner state, and the queen Raj Kanwar Shekhawatji - a Krishna devotee - inspired her husband to build it. Rasik Shiromani Temple was built by Maharaja Sardar Singh (1851-1872). The pair stand inside Ratan Bihari Park on the north side of KEM Road near Junagarh Fort, in red sandstone built in mansion/haveli style: high plinths, pillared galleries, open square and courtyard, ceilings ringed by small chatris with a square canopy at the centre. Date note: one travel site says Ratan Bihari was commissioned in 1846 - flagging the minor conflict; the documented foundation date is Falgun bright-half 3rd, Samvat 1907 (1851 AD).

name: Ratan Bihari Temple
town: Bikaner (Ratan Bihari Park, north side of KEM Road, near Junagarh Fort)
town_description: Bikaner, founded in 1488 by Rao Bika of the Rathore clan, is a historic desert city in northwest Rajasthan famed for the unconquered Junagarh Fort, Lalgarh Palace, its camel-breeding farm, bhujia and old-city havelis; it is a major rail and road hub in the Thar region.

travel.road: Centrally located on KEM Road near Junagarh Fort; easily reached by auto-rickshaw or taxi; pairs well with a Junagarh Fort visit.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning or evening aarti for the best experience.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 5:00 AM - 1:00 PM; evening 5:00 PM - 9:00 PM (promallu.com) - rajasthandhara.com instead gives 7:15 AM - 7:20 PM; conflict, verify on site. Modest dress (cover shoulders and knees); remove shoes.
